definition: Formulate means to work out an idea carefully and put it into exact, systematic form.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word formulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know formulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Between shifts at the observatory, Ho formulated a theory that tied every stray reading of the winter to a single failing sensor.
Sketching is weaker than formulating: a sketch names the plan's big pieces and stops, while formulating works out every piece and fixes the exact wording.
Codify goes further than formulate — a formulated plan is worked out and precisely worded, but a codified one has hardened into official rules that bind everyone after you.

Devise is about inventing the method — a clever way where none existed. Formulate cares less about novelty and more about finish: working the idea out fully and fixing it in exact form. You devise a trick; you formulate a policy.

To draft is to produce a first, rough version, and a draft is allowed to stay loose. Formulating goes to the end of the job: the idea is worked out completely and worded so precisely it could be executed as written.

For a decade the volunteer fire companies along the river ran on habit: everyone knew roughly what to do when the siren went, and roughly was usually enough.
Then two crews arrived at the same grain-elevator fire with opposite ideas about who commanded the scene, and twenty minutes were lost arguing while the roof burned.
The county asked Chief Alma Reyes not to invent anything new, but to formulate what the crews already half-knew: to work the unwritten rules out completely and fix them in exact words.
The result ran nine pages, and every sentence was written so that a captain reading it at 3 a.m.
could act on it without calling anyone.
At the next multi-company fire, command passed in forty seconds, by the book — because now there was a book.
